title: NXT Curator
concept:
=== APPROVED PRODUCT BRIEF (the user picked this from a 5-brief set; build EXACTLY this) ===

Frame: inverted-actor (probability 0.1)
Title: NXT Curator
Thesis: Every AI-to-human handoff is evidence of a catalog knowledge gap; the merchandiser fixes the data, not the conversation.
Why this frame: Inverting the actor from support agent to merchandiser reframes escalation telemetry as a product-data quality signal, surfacing the operational-impact angle: handoffs are bugs in the catalog, not bugs in the bot.

PRIMARY PERSONA:
  Name: Theo Vargas
  Role: Category Merchandiser, Apparel & Footwear
  Context: Owns product data quality for ~14,000 active SKUs across a mid-market omnichannel retailer. Spends mornings in spreadsheets reconciling supplier feeds, afternoons fielding 'why is conversion soft on this line' from his director. The AI shopping assistant launched 6 months ago and now he gets pinged when escalation volume spikes—but nobody has told him WHY.
  Emotional state: Curious but defensive—suspects the catalog is the culprit but has no instrument to prove it; tired of being blamed for things downstream of bad supplier data.
  Pain points:
    - Escalation volume is reported as a single aggregate number with no link to which products or attributes caused it.
    - Supplier feeds arrive with inconsistent or missing attributes (sizing fit, material composition, care instructions) and he can't prioritize which gaps matter.
    - No feedback loop: he fixes an attribute and has no idea if it reduced escalations or improved deflection.
    - Cross-functional friction—support blames the catalog, the AI team blames the model, and he lacks evidence to settle it.
  JTBD: When the AI assistant escalates a shopper question to a human, I want to know exactly which product-data gap caused it so I can patch the catalog and prevent the next hundred escalations.
SECONDARY ACTORS:
  - Support Operations Lead: Consumes deflection forecasts; coordinates agent staffing against predicted escalation volume after catalog fixes ship.
  - AI Assistant Engineering: Owns the model confidence thresholds and consumes Theo's attribute patches into the retrieval knowledge base; receives gap-cluster reports.
  - Supplier Data Onboarding Specialist: Receives prioritized attribute-completeness requests generated from escalation hotspots to push back upstream to vendors.
  - Merchandising Director: Reviews the Catalog Health Scorecard weekly; ties Theo's fixes to conversion and containment KPIs.

DEMONSTRATED MOMENT: Theo opens the weekly Escalation Cause Heatmap, spots a blazing-red cell where the Footwear line intersects the 'sizing fit' attribute, drills in to find 312 handoffs last week all tracing to a missing 'fits true to size' field, patches the attribute inline, and watches the Deflection Impact Estimator project a +9.2pt containment recovery before the change even ships.

USE CASES (12) - the prototype MUST demonstrate at least 5 of these as live flows:
  1. Handoff-Reason Heatmap
     Trigger: Theo logs in Monday morning to his weekly catalog-health review.
     Flow: Lands on the heatmap → product lines on the Y axis, root-cause categories on the X axis, cell intensity = escalation count → he scans for the hottest cells → clicks the Footwear × Sizing cell to drill in.
     AI role: Clusters the prior week's raw handoff events into a stable taxonomy of root-cause categories and maps each to the product line it touched.
     Outcome: Theo instantly sees where AI knowledge fails worst, ranked by volume, without parsing a single transcript.
  2. Knowledge-Gap Clustering
     Trigger: Theo wants to understand the substance of a hot cell beyond the count.
     Flow: From a heatmap cell he opens the cluster view → AI groups the underlying escalations into 3-6 semantic themes → each theme shows a representative paraphrased question and a confidence-drop signature → Theo selects the dominant cluster.
     AI role: Embeds and clusters escalated shopper turns, then names each cluster with a distilled gap description (never a verbatim quote).
     Outcome: Theo learns the escalations aren't random—they're 80% one question shape the catalog can answer.
  3. SKU Escalation Hotspots
     Trigger: Theo needs to know which specific SKUs are driving a cluster.
     Flow: Within a cluster he opens the SKU Drilldown → ranked list of SKUs by escalation contribution → each row shows attribute-completeness score, escalation count, and last supplier-feed date → he sorts by 'fixable now'.
     AI role: Attributes each escalation to the SKU(s) the shopper was viewing or asking about and scores the data completeness of each.
     Outcome: Theo gets a worklist of exact SKUs to fix, prioritized by impact and feasibility.
  4. Missing-Attribute Diagnosis
     Trigger: Theo opens a hotspot SKU to find what specifically is absent.
     Flow: SKU panel shows a field-by-field completeness matrix → missing/low-confidence fields flagged → AI proposes the missing attribute and its likely value from similar SKUs and supplier text → Theo reviews the suggestion.
     AI role: Diagnoses the precise missing or ambiguous attribute and predicts a candidate value with a confidence band and source citation.
     Outcome: Theo no longer guesses what to add—the gap and a probable fix are handed to him.
  5. AI Confidence Decay Tracking
     Trigger: Theo suspects a line's data has degraded over time after a feed change.
     Flow: Opens the confidence trend view for a product line → time-series of average AI answer confidence by attribute → he spots a cliff aligned with a March supplier feed swap → correlates with escalation spike.
     AI role: Tracks rolling AI answer-confidence per attribute and detects step-changes, correlating drops to feed events and escalation surges.
     Outcome: Theo pinpoints the exact upstream change that broke AI knowledge, with a date he can take to the supplier.
  6. Catalog Fix Workflow
     Trigger: Theo decides to patch a diagnosed attribute gap.
     Flow: From the diagnosis he opens the Attribute Fix Editor → accepts or edits the AI-suggested value → applies to one SKU or bulk-applies across the matched cluster → submits to the data pipeline with a change note.
     AI role: Pre-fills the value, validates format against the schema, and identifies all sibling SKUs eligible for the same bulk fix.
     Outcome: Theo ships a fix that resolves the gap for hundreds of SKUs in one action.
  7. Deflection Recovery Forecast
     Trigger: Theo wants to know the payoff before committing a fix.
     Flow: In the Fix Editor a live estimator panel updates as he stages the change → shows projected weekly escalation reduction, deflection-rate delta, and agent-hour savings → he confirms when the number justifies the work.
     AI role: Models the counterfactual escalation volume had the attribute been present, projecting containment recovery with a confidence interval.
     Outcome: Theo makes a data-backed decision and can defend the fix's ROI to his director.
  8. Knowledge-Base Patch Loop
     Trigger: A fix ships and Theo wants to verify it worked.
     Flow: After deploy, the SKU/cluster shows a 'patched' badge → over the following week the actual vs. forecasted deflection appears → Theo reviews accuracy → mis-forecasts feed back to recalibrate the estimator.
     AI role: Re-ingests the patched attribute into the assistant's retrieval base and measures realized escalation change against the forecast.
     Outcome: Theo gets closed-loop proof his fix worked, and the estimator gets sharper over time.
  9. Supplier Gap Escalation
     Trigger: Theo finds a missing attribute he cannot fill himself because the data doesn't exist anywhere.
     Flow: From the diagnosis he flags 'source from supplier' → AI bundles all affected SKUs and the precise field needed → generates a supplier request packet → routes to the onboarding specialist.
     AI role: Composes a structured, supplier-ready data request listing exact fields, affected SKU IDs, and the business impact in escalations.
     Outcome: Theo turns an internal blocker into an actionable upstream ask with quantified urgency.
  10. Weekly Health Briefing
     Trigger: Director asks for the state of catalog data quality at the Monday standup.
     Flow: Theo opens the Catalog Health Scorecard → top-line containment trend, attribute-completeness index, fixes shipped, escalations prevented → exports a one-page summary.
     AI role: Generates a plain-language narrative summary of the week's gaps, fixes, and projected impact (Claude for the prose).
     Outcome: Theo walks into the standup with an authoritative, jargon-free story instead of raw numbers.
  11. Cross-Line Pattern Alert
     Trigger: A new gap pattern emerges that spans multiple product lines.
     Flow: AI detects an attribute gap (e.g. care instructions) recurring across Apparel, Home, and Outdoor → fires an alert in Theo's inbox → he opens a cross-line view → triages a systemic fix.
     AI role: Detects gap signatures that recur across otherwise unrelated lines and elevates them as systemic rather than isolated.
     Outcome: Theo catches structural data problems before they spread, fixing once instead of line-by-line.
  12. Escalation Replay Inspection
     Trigger: Theo needs to validate that a cluster's label truly matches the underlying conversations.
     Flow: From a cluster he opens replay → AI shows paraphrased, de-identified conversation skeletons (intent, the catalog query, the confidence drop point) → Theo confirms or recategorizes the cluster.
     AI role: Renders privacy-safe, distilled conversation skeletons highlighting the exact turn where AI knowledge ran out.
     Outcome: Theo trusts the taxonomy because he can audit it without reading raw, sensitive transcripts.

KEY SCREENS (10) - every screen is a real view, not a placeholder:
  1. Escalation Cause Heatmap - purpose: The home canvas—shows where AI product knowledge fails across the entire catalog at a glance.
     Primary element: A matrix grid: product lines (rows) × root-cause categories (columns), cells color-graded by escalation volume with a week-over-week delta sparkline.
     Motion character: Cells ripple-fade in on load left-to-right; hovering a cell lifts it with a soft shadow and reveals a count tooltip; clicking expands the cell into a drilldown with a spatial zoom.
  2. SKU Drilldown Panel - purpose: Ranks the specific SKUs driving a selected cause cell so Theo gets a prioritized worklist.
     Primary element: A sortable table of SKUs with escalation contribution bars, completeness score chips, and an inline 'fixability' badge.
     Motion character: Slides in from the right as an overlay; rows stagger-cascade; sorting animates rows reordering with FLIP transitions.
  3. Knowledge Gap Cluster View - purpose: Reveals the semantic themes behind escalations so Theo understands the substance, not just the count.
     Primary element: A cluster bubble layout where bubble size = escalation volume and color = AI confidence drop severity, each labeled with a distilled gap description.
     Motion character: Force-directed bubbles settle into place with gentle physics; selecting a bubble pulses it and dims the rest.
  4. Attribute Fix Editor - purpose: Where Theo patches the missing or ambiguous attribute, with AI-suggested values and bulk-apply scope.
     Primary element: A split panel: left = field completeness matrix with the gap highlighted; right = editable value field pre-filled with AI suggestion plus a bulk-scope selector.
     Motion character: AI suggestion types in character-by-character; accepting snaps a green confirmation pill; bulk-scope toggle expands a count of affected SKUs with a counting-up number.
  5. Deflection Impact Estimator - purpose: Projects the escalation reduction and deflection recovery of a staged fix before it ships.
     Primary element: A live gauge plus a forecast line chart showing current vs. projected deflection rate with a shaded confidence band.
     Motion character: The gauge needle sweeps to the projected value as Theo stages a change; the forecast line draws on with an easing animation and the delta number counts up.
  6. Confidence Decay Timeline - purpose: Shows how AI answer confidence for an attribute has drifted over time, correlated to feed events.
     Primary element: A multi-line time-series with annotated event markers (feed swaps, fixes) and an escalation overlay band.
     Motion character: Lines animate left-to-right on load; event markers drop in with a subtle bounce; hovering an event reveals a correlation callout.
  7. Catalog Health Scorecard - purpose: The executive-readable summary of data quality, fixes shipped, and escalations prevented.
     Primary element: A KPI tile row (completeness index, containment rate, fixes shipped, escalations prevented) above an AI-written narrative briefing.
     Motion character: Tiles flip-reveal sequentially; the narrative text fades in paragraph by paragraph; the export button has a satisfying press-down state.
  8. Cross-Line Pattern Alert Inbox - purpose: Surfaces systemic gap patterns spanning multiple product lines as actionable alerts.
     Primary element: A stacked card feed where each card shows the gap signature, affected lines, and projected impact, with triage actions.
     Motion character: New alert cards slide in from the top with a gentle attention pulse; dismissing a card swipes it off with momentum.
  9. Escalation Replay Inspector - purpose: Lets Theo audit a cluster's accuracy by reviewing privacy-safe conversation skeletons.
     Primary element: A vertical conversation skeleton showing intent → catalog query → confidence-drop turn, with the failure point marked.
     Motion character: Turns reveal top-to-bottom as a guided walkthrough; the confidence-drop turn highlights with a red pulse when reached.
  10. Supplier Request Composer - purpose: Bundles unfillable gaps into a structured supplier data request with quantified business impact.
     Primary element: A generated request packet preview listing exact fields, affected SKU IDs, and escalation impact, with a route-to-onboarding action.
     Motion character: Packet assembles section by section with a drafting shimmer; the send action collapses the panel into a confirmation toast.

AI CAPABILITIES (8) - every one wires to a real /api/ai/* endpoint via the multi-provider fallback helper:
  1. Escalation Root-Cause Clustering
     User action: Theo opens the heatmap or a cluster view for any product line.
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: De-identified escalated conversation turns, the SKU(s) in context, AI confidence scores at the handoff turn, and attribute metadata.
     Output: A stable taxonomy of root-cause categories with each escalation assigned, plus per-cluster distilled gap descriptions.
     User benefit: Theo sees the structural reason behind hundreds of escalations without reading any transcripts.
  2. Catalog Gap Detection
     User action: Theo opens a SKU drilldown or the diagnosis panel.
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: SKU attribute records, the canonical attribute schema for the category, supplier feed text, and the escalation cluster context.
     Output: A field-by-field completeness diagnosis flagging missing or low-confidence attributes ranked by escalation impact.
     User benefit: Theo knows exactly which field to fix instead of guessing across thousands of SKUs.
  3. Deflection Impact Modeling
     User action: Theo stages an attribute fix in the editor.
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: Historical escalation volume for the attribute, the fix scope (SKU count), realized deflection rates from prior similar fixes.
     Output: A projected weekly escalation reduction, deflection-rate delta, and agent-hour savings with a confidence interval.
     User benefit: Theo can justify and prioritize fixes by their forecasted payoff before doing the work. THIS IS THE HEADLINE AHA.
  4. Attribute Suggestion Engine
     User action: Theo opens the Fix Editor on a SKU with a missing attribute.
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: The target SKU, similar sibling SKUs with the attribute populated, supplier description text, and category norms.
     Output: A candidate attribute value with a confidence band and a source citation for traceability.
     User benefit: Theo accepts a probable correct value in one click rather than researching it manually.
  5. Confidence Trend Analysis
     User action: Theo opens the confidence decay timeline for a product line.
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: Time-series of AI answer confidence per attribute, supplier feed event log, escalation counts.
     Output: Detected step-changes in confidence aligned to feed events, with a correlation strength score.
     User benefit: Theo pinpoints the exact upstream change that degraded AI knowledge, with a date for the supplier.
  6. Weekly Briefing Composer
     User action: Theo opens or exports the Catalog Health Scorecard.
     Model: Claude Opus 4.7
     Input: The week's gap clusters, fixes shipped, projected and realized impact, and KPI deltas.
     Output: A plain-language one-page narrative summarizing the state of catalog data quality and recommended next actions.
     User benefit: Theo walks into the standup with an authoritative, jargon-free story rather than raw metrics.
  7. Privacy-Safe Conversation Distillation
     User action: Theo opens the Escalation Replay Inspector for a cluster.
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: Raw escalated conversation logs containing potential PII and shopper context.
     Output: De-identified conversation skeletons reduced to intent, catalog query, and the confidence-drop turn—no verbatim shopper text over 80 chars.
     User benefit: Theo audits clustering accuracy without ever touching sensitive raw transcripts.
  8. Schema-Grounded Validation
     User action: Theo submits an attribute fix or bulk patch.
     Model: Wiki RAG
     Input: The canonical category attribute schema, allowed value enumerations, and formatting rules.
     Output: A validation pass/fail with format normalization and any conflicting-value warnings across bulk-scoped SKUs.
     User benefit: Theo's fixes are guaranteed schema-clean before they reach the live knowledge base.

VISUAL DIRECTION:
  Aesthetic keywords: data-dense editorial restraint, analytical confidence, signal-over-noise dashboards, warm-neutral canvas with high-contrast diagnostic accents, the feeling of a quant terminal designed by a magazine art director
  Hero treatment: The Escalation Cause Heatmap is the hero—a large, breathing matrix that fills the canvas with calm authority, product lines down the left in a clean serif, root-cause columns across the top, cells graded in a perceptually-uniform red-to-cool scale. Generous whitespace frames the grid so the hot cells read instantly as the story. A thin sidebar carries the worklist; everything else recedes. The composition should feel like the front page of a financial broadsheet—dense but legible, hierarchical, unhurried.
  Motion character: Purposeful and physical—elements settle rather than pop. Heatmap cells ripple in on load; drilldowns use spatial zoom so Theo never loses his place; forecast numbers count up to give weight to outcomes; patched cells cool down with smooth gradient transitions to reward the fix. Nothing bounces gratuitously; motion always communicates causality.
  Image generation prompts (the prototype should call /api/ai/gemini-image at runtime with these - the runner reads the result and renders it as a hero/empty-state/illustration):
    1. A perceptually-uniform red-to-cool heatmap matrix on a warm-neutral canvas, editorial dashboard style, generous whitespace, thin serif row labels — for the hero empty-state backdrop
    2. An abstract cluster-bubble field with soft physics-settled circles in graded confidence colors, analytical and calm — for the Knowledge Gap Cluster View loading state
    3. A clean line-chart time-series with annotated event markers and a shaded escalation band, financial-broadsheet aesthetic — for the Confidence Decay Timeline header
    4. A minimalist gauge sweeping toward a positive delta with a soft glow, restrained quant-terminal style — for the Deflection Impact Estimator hero moment
    5. A flat-illustration of a single highlighted catalog field rippling outward to hundreds of connected product cards, communicating one-fix-many-SKUs — for the bulk-apply confirmation
    6. An executive scorecard layout with flip-reveal KPI tiles in warm neutrals with high-contrast accents — for the Catalog Health Scorecard

FEATURE ROADMAP (3 phases) - the prototype demonstrates Phase 1 in working code; later phases appear as roadmap surfaces inside the experience:
  1. Phase 1 (Weeks 1-3) - Foundations — See the Gaps
     • Escalation event ingestion pipeline with SKU and confidence tagging
     • Root-cause taxonomy clustering on de-identified turns
     • Escalation Cause Heatmap as the home canvas
     • SKU Drilldown Panel with completeness scoring
     • Privacy-safe conversation distillation for replay
     • Catalog attribute schema integration (Wiki RAG validation)
     Success: Theo can trace any escalation spike to a specific product line × root-cause cell within 30 seconds, with 90% of events auto-categorized.
  2. Phase 2 (Month 2) - Intelligence — Diagnose and Fix
     • Attribute Suggestion Engine with confidence and source citation
     • Attribute Fix Editor with bulk-scope apply
     • Deflection Impact Estimator with live forecasting
     • Knowledge-Base Patch Loop with realized-vs-forecast tracking
     • Confidence Decay Timeline correlated to feed events
     • Supplier Request Composer for unfillable gaps
     Success: Median time from gap detection to shipped fix under 10 minutes; forecast accuracy within ±2pt of realized deflection on verified fixes.
  3. Phase 3 (Quarter 2) - Scale — Systemic and Proactive
     • Cross-Line Pattern Alert detection and inbox
     • AI-written Weekly Health Briefing (Claude) with export
     • Catalog Health Scorecard with executive KPIs
     • Automated supplier-feed regression alerts
     • Multi-provider AI fallback (Gemini primary, Claude secondary) for resilience
     • Self-recalibrating estimator from accumulated fix outcomes
     Success: 30% reduction in total weekly AI-to-human escalations attributable to catalog fixes, with a 5pt lift in overall containment rate.

NARRATIVE ARC (7 beats) - the multi-timeframe user journey the prototype must SUGGEST through copy, seed data, and roadmap surfaces:
  1. Minute 1
     User: Theo opens NXT Curator for the first time and lands on the heatmap, immediately spotting a blazing-red Footwear × Sizing cell.
     AI: The system has already clustered last week's escalations into a clean taxonomy and rendered the cell intensity.
     Feeling: Validation—'I knew it was the catalog, and now I can see it.'
  2. Minute 5
     User: He drills into the hot cell and finds 312 escalations all tracing to a missing 'fits true to size' field on 214 SKUs.
     AI: Gap detection isolates the exact attribute and suggests 'Fits true to size' at 88% confidence with a source citation.
     Feeling: Clarity—'It's one field. One field caused all of this.'
  3. Minute 8
     User: Theo accepts the suggestion, bulk-applies it across 214 SKUs, and watches the estimator project +9.2pt deflection recovery.
     AI: The estimator models the counterfactual and the schema validator confirms the patch is clean.
     Feeling: Power—'I just fixed hundreds of escalations in one click and I can prove the payoff.'
  4. Day 1
     User: Theo works down a prioritized worklist of the next five hottest cells, shipping fixes for material and care attributes.
     AI: Each fix re-ingests into the assistant's retrieval base and queues realized-impact tracking.
     Feeling: Momentum—'This is the most productive afternoon I've had in months.'
  5. Week 1
     User: He returns to find the patched cells have cooled and the verified deflection landed within 2pt of the forecast.
     AI: The patch loop reports realized impact and recalibrates the estimator slightly.
     Feeling: Trust—'The forecasts are real. I can plan around these.'
  6. Month 1
     User: Theo gets a cross-line alert that a care-instructions gap is recurring across Apparel and Home and triages a systemic fix.
     AI: Pattern detection elevates the recurring signature as systemic and quantifies projected impact.
     Feeling: Foresight—'I'm catching problems before they spread now.'
  7. Month 3+
     User: Theo walks into the director standup with an AI-written briefing showing a 30% escalation drop tied to his catalog fixes.
     AI: Claude composes the narrative; the scorecard ties fixes to containment and conversion lift.
     Feeling: Authority—'I'm no longer blamed for escalations; I'm the reason they're falling.'

INTERACTION CHOREOGRAPHY (10 beats) - the step-by-step script for the HEADLINE aha interaction; honor the timing_ms values where given:
  1. Theo clicks the blazing-red Footwear × Sizing & Fit cell on the heatmap.
     System: The cell expands into a spatial-zoom drilldown overlay loading the SKU contributors.
     Motion/feedback: Cell lifts and scales toward center; background dims; loading shimmer on the SKU table. (450ms)
  2. He scans the SKU Drilldown showing SKU-FW-0148 at 312 escalations, completeness 0.61.
     System: Rows cascade in sorted by escalation contribution with completeness chips and fixability badges.
     Motion/feedback: Staggered row reveal; the top contributing bar pulses subtly once. (600ms)
  3. Theo clicks 'Diagnose gap' on the top SKU.
     System: The diagnosis panel slides in showing the field-completeness matrix with 'sizing_fit' flagged red.
     Motion/feedback: Panel slides from right; the missing field cell flashes red then settles. (400ms)
  4. He reads the AI suggestion: 'Fits true to size' at 88% confidence with a source link.
     System: The suggested value types into the field with a confidence band and citation chip.
     Motion/feedback: Character-by-character type-in; confidence band fills left-to-right. (700ms)
  5. Theo expands the bulk-scope selector.
     System: The system identifies 214 sibling SKUs eligible for the same fix and shows the count.
     Motion/feedback: Scope panel unfolds; the affected-SKU number counts up from 1 to 214. (500ms)
  6. He toggles 'Apply to all 214'.
     System: The Deflection Impact Estimator panel activates and begins forecasting.
     Motion/feedback: Estimator gauge wakes with a soft glow; forecast chart axes draw in. (350ms)
  7. Theo watches the forecast resolve.
     System: The gauge needle sweeps to +9.2pt deflection recovery and the projection line draws on.
     Motion/feedback: Needle sweeps with easing; forecast line animates with a shaded confidence band; the delta number counts up to +9.2. (900ms)
  8. He clicks 'Validate'.
     System: Schema validation runs against the category attribute spec and returns clean.
     Motion/feedback: A green check ripples across the field matrix; a 'schema clean' pill appears. (400ms)
  9. Theo clicks 'Ship fix'.
     System: The patch submits to the data pipeline and queues knowledge-base re-ingestion.
     Motion/feedback: Button presses down; a progress arc completes; confirmation toast slides in: '214 SKUs patched — tracking impact.' (600ms)
  10. He returns to the heatmap.
     System: The previously red cell shows a 'patched' badge and a forecasted cool-down preview.
     Motion/feedback: Cell color eases from red toward amber with a gentle gradient transition; badge fades in. (700ms)

SUCCESS CRITERIA (Stage 5 audits the prototype against each of these):
  - Theo can trace any escalation spike to a specific product line and root-cause attribute within 30 seconds of login.
  - At least 90% of escalation events are auto-categorized into the root-cause taxonomy without manual tagging.
  - Median time from gap detection to a shipped catalog fix is under 10 minutes.
  - Deflection forecasts land within ±2 percentage points of realized impact on verified fixes.
  - A single bulk-apply action can patch an attribute across 100+ sibling SKUs in one operation.
  - No raw shopper transcript or PII is ever exposed in the merchandiser interface—only distilled, de-identified skeletons.
  - Within one quarter, catalog fixes drive a measurable reduction in total weekly escalations attributable to data gaps.

  Brand: NXT — analytical, trustworthy, editorial; warm-neutral palette with diagnostic accent colors

    - All AI-suggested attribute values must carry a confidence score and source citation before being acceptable

=== ORIGINAL ENGAGEMENT CONTEXT (the rich consulting brief the briefs were generated from) ===
Design a concrete AI system architecture and interaction flow that preserves shopper context and product knowledge during a seamless handoff from AI assistant to human agent. Detail the data schema required to pass session state, the trigger conditions for escalation, and the agent-side interface that displays the summarized conversation history.

brief.one_line_thesis: Every AI-to-human handoff is evidence of a catalog knowledge gap; the merchandiser fixes the data, not the conversation.

primary_persona.name: Theo Vargas
primary_persona.context: Owns product data quality for ~14,000 active SKUs across a mid-market omnichannel retailer. Spends mornings in spreadsheets reconciling supplier feeds, afternoons fielding 'why is conversion soft on this line' from his director. The AI shopping assistant launched 6 months ago and now he gets pinged when escalation volume spikes—but nobody has told him WHY.
primary_persona.emotional_state: Curious but defensive—suspects the catalog is the culprit but has no instrument to prove it; tired of being blamed for things downstream of bad supplier data.

secondary_actors.involvement: Consumes deflection forecasts; coordinates agent staffing against predicted escalation volume after catalog fixes ship.
Owns the model confidence thresholds and consumes Theo's attribute patches into the retrieval knowledge base; receives gap-cluster reports.
Receives prioritized attribute-completeness requests generated from escalation hotspots to push back upstream to vendors.
Reviews the Catalog Health Scorecard weekly; ties Theo's fixes to conversion and containment KPIs.

jobs_to_be_done: When the AI assistant escalates a shopper question to a human, I want to know exactly which product-data gap caused it so I can patch the catalog and prevent the next hundred escalations.

brand_application.logo_treatment: NXT custom vector wordmark (BRAND_LOGO_SVG) rendered at masthead height 26px; CSS color: ink #141414 on light surfaces, paper #FFFFFF on the #0D0D0D rail. Chartreuse #B8B800 fill reserved only for an active-state masthead accent rule, never the wordmark body. Set on near-white pale canvas #FAFAF7 with a 1px hairline #DDDDD6 rule beneath. Never a letter-in-a-box.
brand_application.voice_tone: Editorial, analytical, front-page-of-the-FT density. Trustworthy and unhurried; every label earns its keep. Plain-language conclusions over jargon — the title carries the finding, the number is evidence. Diagnostic, not decorative.

display.usage: Hero matrix title, screen mastheads (Escalation Cause Heatmap), KPI hero numerals capped at 36px in body weight as evidence — never out-ranking the action title.

body.usage: Cluster theme descriptions, distilled gap reasons (≤80 chars), AI narrative briefing paragraphs, action-title conclusion sentences at 46px weight 600.

label.usage: Column headers (root-cause categories), row labels, meta chips, SKU IDs, timestamps, fixability badges. Kicker variant: uppercase, tracking 4px, cyan #00B7C3, reserved for the single section kicker per surface.

quote.usage: Distilled representative intent on cluster bubbles and replay skeletons (de-identified, ≤80 chars, never verbatim). Numbers ride inside cited claims per Quantitative Claim Rule.

data.usage: Escalation cell counts, completeness scores, deflection delta (+9.2pt), counting-up bulk SKU count (1→214), confidence scores. Tabular figures so columns align in the matrix. Capped below the 46px title.

color_system._heatmap_scale_note: Colorblind-safe perceptually-uniform sequential scale (NOT red/green). Cool→hot via a single-hue-rotation ramp anchored on brand tokens: healthy/empty = ecru #F2F1EA → cool low = wash-cool #EBF7F8 → cyan #00B7C3 → teal-dark #0B3A3D mid → rust #CC6644 hot → error #FF5A5A blazing. Severity ALSO encoded by mono numeral + symbol in every cell (WCAG 1.4.1, deuteranopia-safe). Patched cool-down eases hot→ecru, never red→green.
color_system._usage_discipline: Chartreuse #B8B800 appears on ONE primary CTA per screen (Ship fix) + masthead accent rule only; <15% of surface. Cyan #00B7C3 reserved for evidence/citation panels and opportunity signals. Rust #CC6644 = friction/warning (one negative hue, differentiated by icon+title). Rail #0D0D0D for the sidebar worklist spine. NEVER flood accent as background.

critique.summary: The merged single-file prototype is internally coherent and shippable. The App root is correctly named and mounts every declared Screen_x via state.activeScreen with a working Rail navigation. All nine screens reference state keys present in initialState and dispatch only actions the reducer handles; I traced each ACTION in the switch and each screen's dispatch calls and found no orphaned keys or unhandled actions. Seed data is deep and concrete: named protagonist Theo Vargas, 28 SKUs, 6 gap clusters, 6 attribute gaps, 4 catalog fixes, 3 feed events, 3 pattern alerts, two full confidence-trend series, and a populated KPI set with real numbers (312 escalations, +9.2pt, 214 SKUs). Brand tokens, fonts, colorblind-safe heatmap ramp with glyph+numeral encoding, de-identification banners, provenance chips, and read-only gating are consistently applied. Runtime contract is obeyed: global hooks (useState/useReducer/useEffect/useMemo/useRef) are used without React destructuring, framer-motion via window.framerMotion, icons via window.lucide, no import/export, no render/createRoot. The one mild oddity is in Screen_confidence_timeline where a nested function sevGlyphSafe is referenced before its hoisted declaration and a stray empty sevGlyph ternary — but function declarations hoist within their scope so this executes without error, and a duplicate overlapping CLIFF text element is harmless. No blocker-level integration drift was found, so the assembled file ships verbatim.
